item.description: Job Details: Schedule: Monday through Thursday from 4:40 am to 2:40 pm or until complete. Some Friday work may be required based upon trial needs. Work schedule is subject to change based upon production needs. Join the Cobb Family and Grow With Us! At Cobb, we’re passionate about helping our team members thrive—both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you and your family in every stage of life. The best part- you’re eligible for benefits on day 1 of full time hire! Starting Pay : $17.00 per hour plus additional shift differential for evenings, nights and weekends. What’s in it for you? Our competitive benefits include: Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance Short-Term & Long-Term Disability Free Telehealth Services Free Mental Health Services Well-Being Support Programs 401K & Stock Options Company Paid Life Insurance Free Education starting your first day on 175 -degree programs Citizenship Assistance Discounts on thousands of programs and services through Beneplace Additionally, we offer incentives such as Cobb Rewards, New Hire Referral and Referral Bonuses, Paid Vacations, Paid Holidays, Overtime Eligibility, and Earned Time Off. These are just a few of the ways we invest in YOU. Ready to take the next step? Apply today and become part of the Cobb family! Priority consideration will be provided to internal applicants first. Applicants with previous agricultural or production experience will be considered preferred. Applicants must reside in the United States to be considered for an interview. Requirements: Must have at least 12 months of consecutive work history with one employer and no additional job gaps in employment greater than 6 months in the past 36 months. If applicant has been laid off or providing child or elder care, the employment gap will be increased to 18 months. Previous work history will not apply to applicants who have been full time students consecutively for the last 36 months. Rehire criteria is a minimum waiting period of 180 days. Rehire Rule of no more than 3 times worked at Cobb/Tyson Foods. Company: Cobb Position Summary: This position is responsible for handling birds and equipment for selection process by performing all essential duties in rotation with others. Other duties may be assigned. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Prepare and setup for selection process by loading coops and equipment into truck/trailer for transport to brothe oding area and unload at the designated house, setup equipment for selection process per instructions (10%) Select birds by performing the following duties: Isolate no more than 200 birds into catch frame for selection as many times as necessary until all birds are selected; catch birds per animal welfare standards; identify gender; verify line by observing wing band color; hold clean wing band under scanner for data entry; place bird in scale cone to obtain weight repeating multiple times until complete; monitor bird groups and “stir” to avoid crowding per animal welfare guidelines; place birds received from selector in designated location such as market pen, breeder candidate coop per gender, full dissect, leg dissect based upon characteristics as instructed by selector. If designated as market remove wing bands and mark head with colored food grade dye prior to placing in area designated for market birds multiple times until complete (60%) Load, transport, and unload coops of birds to feed conversion house and/or dissection lab (10%) Euthanize off condition birds using the cervical dislocation method based upon animal welfare guidelines (10%) Other duties, responsibilities, and activities: Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice. Such as: Move partitions, back trailer, clean and sanitize equipment for movement between areas per biosecurity requirements, operate a high pressure and regular water hose, maintain equipment by checking fluid levels, filters, tire pressure, and clean/disinfect to remove debris, maintains foot pans and hand sanitizer, maintains a clean and organized work area. (10%) Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements: The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines. Physical Demands and Work Environment: Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly catch, carry, and control individual birds weighing from 3.5 to 12 pounds , lift and move empty coops weighing up to 16 pounds each, buddy lift and carry coops with birds weighing up to 88 pounds , and pull/push stacks of coops with birds weighing up to 360 pounds . While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift (concrete floor); walk; sit; use hands to handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; stoop; talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus. Tools and Equipment: Requires use of hand tools such as wire cutters, pliers, wrenches, broom, squeegee, shovel, counter; power tools such as cordless drill; equipment such as catch frames, scales, tables, scanners, extension cords, coops; safe operation of vehicle to and from work area. Environment: Required to work on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, dusty, wet and cold environments. Personal Protective Equipment Required: safety goggles and/or glasses, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, and rubber boots are required. Must wear company provided facial covering. Ear plugs, arm protectors, and NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators may be worn as desired. Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants, vehicle fluids, and lubricants. Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks. item.description: Centene is transforming the health of our communities one person at a time. As an Executive on our team, you could be the one who changes everything for our 28 million members. Position Purpose: Serve as a liaison to state government entities to improve the legislative and regulatory environment for the state health plan and Centene Corporation Assist with the development of state legislative public policy concerning state insurance, Managed Care Organization and Medicare and Medicaid regulations through the initiatives of state legislators and their staff. Develop strategic relationships with state legislative policymakers to enhance the health plan and Centene’s role as a partner with the state and to assist in shaping public policy initiatives. Identify, evaluate and analyze the impact of state legislative and regulatory issues for state health plan and Centene Corporation and advise management concerning their impact. Represent and serve as point person for the state health plan and Centene Corporation to outside trade groups/stakeholders including state AHIP organization, state medical association, state hospital association and related Medicare and Medicaid business vendors. Represent state health plan and Centene Corporation to state legislators and their staffs. Develop and shape legislative policies and strategies through relevant coalitions and issue advocacy campaigns. item.title: Source Selection Advisor Sme
item.description: Position Summary Hive Group, a HUBZone-certified SDVOSB and multiple award-winning organization, delivers innovative solutions for complex, mission-critical federal programs. We are seeking a highly skilled Source Selection Advisor - Subject Matter Expert to provide senior leader advisory support and strategic oversight for the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Technical Advisory and Assistance Services (TACS) program located at Redstone Arsenal Huntsville AL. In this high-visibility role, you will act as the principal advisor to Source Selection Evaluation Boards (SSEBs), Advisory Councils (SSACs), and Source Selection Authorities (SSAs) across multiple complex, multi-million-dollar defense acquisitions. You will perform independent, high-level analyses of source selection schedules, documentation, and processes to forecast risk and ensure strict compliance with DoD and MDA Source Selection Procedures. This position is tailored for a seasoned acquisition executive with a background equivalent to a GS-15 or senior military leader. You will shape the future of agency procurement by collaborating with the Enterprise Procurement Innovation Cell (EPIC) to research and deploy cutting-edge contracting solutions. If you hold a Bachelor's degree, a DAWIA Level III certification, and have a proven track record of successfully guiding senior leaders through complex FAR Part 15 source selections and formal contract protests, we invite you to lead this vital enterprise mission. This role requires an Active TS/SCI Personnel are required to be on-site at Redstone Arsenal AL. Key Responsibilities Provide source selection senior leader advisory support, to include independent review of: Source Selection Plans (SSP), solicitations, exchanges with Industry, review of source selection documentation (e.g., Evaluation Notices (ENs), Competitive Range Decision Documents (CRDD), Proposal Analysis Reports (PAR), Source Selection Decision Documents (SSDD), and associated competitive range and decision briefings) and debriefings in accordance with the DoD and MDA Source Selection Procedures, including MDA Instruction 5013.06-INS. Collaborate simultaneously with multiple Source Selection Evaluation Boards (SSEBs), Source Selection Advisory Councils (SSACs), and Source Selection Authorities (SSAs) to identify potential problem areas and advise source selection teams in matters related to the development of solicitations, evaluation of proposals, exchanges with industry, and evaluation documents. Conduct independent senior analysis of source selection schedules, solicitation documentation, processes, or procedures to inform the SSA, SSAC, SSEB, PCO, Source Selection Director, or other cleared personnel, of any associated risks or potential impacts. Assist the Source Selection Directorate in development of source selection templates, dissemination of best practices and lessons learned, and conducting research and outreach on source selection topics and other related topics, as required. Develop and deliver general and procurement-specific source selection training, Directorate Enterprise Procurement Innovation Cell (EPIC) related training, conduct any other required miscellaneous training, and participate in Government teleconferences, meetings, or out-briefs, as required. Assist the EPIC in conducting research, developing proposed courses of action, outreach to other Government entities for collaborative purposes, development of contracting innovation processes and procedures, and dissemination of best practices and lessons learned as required. Qualifications ACTIVE TS/SCI Required. Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Contract Management or equivalent field. Prior experience as a GS-15, or equivalent positions in the military, a DoD buying activity or civilian agency which executed assisted acquisitions on behalf of DoD activities. Minimum of 10 years of prior experience as a warranted contracting officer or program manager in a DoD buying activity, or civilian agency which executed assisted acquisitions on behalf of DoD activities. DAWIA Level III Certification in Contracting or Program Management. Direct experience in advising and/or conducting/leading more than five (5) source selections, including one or more procurement protests within DoD, or a civilian agency in support of DoD activities/agencies. Experience with FAR Part 15 formal source selection procedures, FAR Subpart 16.505 ordering procedures; and FAR Part 33.1. Demonstrated experience and capability to advise the federal government on all aspects of the acquisition life cycle to implement and adopt innovative acquisition solutions. Compensation and Benefits The estimated compensation range for this position is between $223,700 - $247,300 annually. Actual salary is determined by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s specialized skills, certifications, and years of experience. Hive Group offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance (medical, dental, vision), life and disability insurance, retirement contributions, paid leave, federal holidays, professional development opportunities, and lifestyle benefits. A Commitment to Equal Opportunity Hive Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer dedicated to fair and unbiased employment decisions. We do not discriminate based on race, color, sex (including gender and transgender status), age, religion, national origin, disability, marital status, veteran status, domestic partner or civil union status, gender identity, medical condition, genetic information, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, and local laws. Our hiring and promotion decisions are based exclusively on an individual's qualifications and suitability for the role. Protecting Your Information Stay vigilant against fraudulent job offers and individuals impersonating Hive Group Talent Acquisition Specialists. Hive Group will never request payment details or money during the application process. Official communications will only come from email addresses ending in @hive-llc.com or @applytojob.com — not from free email services like Gmail or messaging platforms such as WhatsApp. If you receive suspicious messages requesting payment or personal information, please report them immediately to [email protected] .

item.title: Director Of Government Affairs
item.description: Reports to: Vice President of Government Affairs Status: Full-time; Exempt Location : Washington D.C. This is a hybrid workplace, with Mondays and Wednesdays in the office and three days remote, as well as the occasional need to work in person for events and special projects. Overtime Status : Exempt Salary: $145K-$179K About Groundwork Collaborative Launched in 2018, Groundwork Collaborative is driven by the idea that We Are The Economy: when all of us are doing well, that is when our economy thrives. We fight for progressive economic policy and narrative change that builds accountable public power, breaks up concentrations of private power, and affirmatively centers people too long left out of prosperity. We understand that taken together, these actions will lead to a stronger and more resilient economy. Groundwork’s unique structure – part strategic communications, part think tank, and part issue advocacy organization – allows us to drive narrative and policy change with credibility, expertise, and impact. We work across four core audiences – the media, policymakers, economic experts, and grasstops leaders – and use targeted policy campaigns and timely research and messaging to advance a truly inclusive economic worldview. Position Summary This is a pivotal moment for economic policymaking. As Groundwork’s Director of Government Affairs, you will lead direct, substantive engagement with Congress and the executive branch, shape the strategy for how we engage with policymakers, and connect Groundwork’s experts, research, and messaging with the lawmakers and staff who need them. Reporting to the Vice President of Government Affairs, you will serve as a senior member of Groundwork’s Partnerships and Influence team. As Groundwork’s Director of Government Affairs, you will… Partner with the Vice President of Government Affairs and Associate Director of Congressional Affairs to design and drive an outreach strategy that advances both immediate and long-term economic policy priorities. Broaden and deepen relationships with congressional committees and offices to amplify Groundwork’s core messages. Serve as Groundwork’s liaison to the federal government, spotting and seizing opportunities for strategic engagement. Craft sharp, persuasive materials for policymakers and their staff including but not limited to talking points, fact sheets, letters, testimony, and more. Lead meetings, briefings, hearing prep, and other high-stakes engagement with government officials and staff. Keep colleagues informed on legislative and executive branch activity. Proactively communicate across internal and external stakeholders. Support and mentor staff members, especially those on the Partnerships and Influence team. Serve as a trusted thought partner and technical resource to the team and organizational leadership on all things government. Move fast when news breaks, analyzing and responding to Congressional and executive developments in real time. Qualifications You bring relevant experience in government relations, legislative work on the Hill, congressional affairs work in the executive branch, and/or government affairs work at a nonprofit organization. You are experienced in preparing witnesses for congressional committee hearings. You have a commitment to creating a just, inclusive, and robust economy that delivers opportunity and dignity to all. You bring a strong familiarity with federal economic policymaking institutions (including Congress, executive branch agencies, and the White House). You bring existing government staff relationships and policy coalition networks. You write and speak with clarity and persuasion. You are highly organized and thrive driving work forward under tight deadlines in a fast paced environment. You think creatively and bring an entrepreneurial drive to developing new strategies that secure advocacy wins. You have experience interfacing directly and managing relationships with government officials and senior staff. Research shows that candidates from underrepresented backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every qualification. If this role excites you and you meet most — but not all — of these criteria, we encourage you to apply. The salary range for this role is $145,000 - $179,000 annually. We offer a generous benefits package, including five weeks of vacation and personal leave, two week-long office closures, additional time off for floating and federal holidays, zero-premium health insurance, a generous HRA, a retirement contribution of up to 6%, up to 16 weeks parental leave, and health club and cell-phone reimbursements, among other benefits. We are a hybrid workplace, with two days a week in the office and three days remote, as well as the occasional need to work in person for events and special projects. Groundwork is a unionized workplace and is represented by the Nonprofit Professional Employees Union (NPEU). This position is not in the bargaining unit. How to apply To begin the application process, please submit an application on our career page, including a resume and cover letter. The cover letter should describe your specific experience related to this position and what excites you about this work Thank you for your interest!
item.dc:creator: Groundwork Collaborative

item.title: Economic Policy Program Fall Internship
item.description: BPC's Fall Internship Program BPC's internship program in the fall will be in-person with on-site work on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursdays at BPC’s office located at 1225 I (Eye) Street in Washington, DC. Fall interns work 18-20 hours per week and will receive a $3,000 stipend for ten weeks of work. Interns must be juniors or above. Applicants must currently be enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate program, or a recent graduate. Interns will provide functional support, conduct research, and work directly with policy analysts and staff in various capacities. Our Fall Internship program starts on Monday, September 14, 2026, and ends Friday, November 20, 2026 Relocation assistance will not be provided. Project Description: BPC's Economic Policy Program (EPP) develops bipartisan policy recommendations designed to enhance the economic opportunity, prosperity, and security of the American people. EPP continues to be a trusted leader in the analysis of federal fiscal policy, encompassing the areas of debt, tax reform, appropriations and the federal budget process, and retirement and financial security. EPP’s is known for its analysis of the federal debt limit, a project that was initially led by now Federal Reserve Chairman Jay Powell during his time as a Fellow at BPC. Subsequent analyses have long been widely cited both in the media and directly by policymakers. Our team also provides research, analysis, and commentary on the major fiscal and budget debates occurring at any given time in Washington, from the implementation of the Fiscal Responsibility Act’s spending caps to the risks and harms of government shutdowns to the future trajectory of U.S. government finances. EPP’s tax portfolio seeks bipartisan reform that will create opportunities for businesses of all sizes, support workers and families, and improve our nation’s fiscal outlook in the years to come. We are especially focused on opportunities for fiscally responsible tax reform. Our work on retirement and financial security focuses on policies that expand access to well-designed retirement savings vehicles, help Americans preserve their retirement income, and resolve Social Security’s structural imbalance to avoid harmful and abrupt benefit cuts when the program’s trust fund is depleted. We continue to play a prominent role in informing and promoting legislative progress on private-sector savings, working to advance reforms that help Americans create financial security through emergency savings accounts, savings for retirement, and other government assistance to promote economic growth and stability. In 2022, EPP acquired and relaunched the American Savings Education Council (ASEC), a unique cross-sector public-private partnership originally formed in 1994 by the U.S. Department of Labor and Employee Benefit Research Institute. In convening with our partners, we seek to address the nation’s most pressing financial security challenges through research, collaboration, and policy innovation. Responsibilities: The intern will be working closely with all the policy experts across our team, reporting to the program manager. Responsibilities will vary day-to-day, but may include: Support long-term policy projects and papers by conducting background research and writing Draft blog posts and assist staff in preparing responses to Hill and media requests Monitor major congressional activity, analyzing budget documents Take notes at Congressional hearings and external events Event planning, program management, and administrative tasks Qualifications: Must be an enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate school or be a recent graduate Strong research and writing skills Ability to communicate clearly and effectively An interest and experience in fiscal and economic policy topics, such as tax policy, retirement savings, and federal budget policy Strong research and data analysis skills; proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Suite preferred Application Process: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until a qualified candidate has been identified Please do not send multiple submissions Incomplete applications will not be considered No phone calls, please Non-U.S. citizens are eligible to apply but must have a valid work permit or visa verifying eligibility to work in the United States We do not offer visa sponsorship Required materials (if possible, please submit as one PDF File): Resume Cover Letter Relevant writing sample (3-5 pages) College or university transcript (unofficial is acceptable) Brief response to the statement "What does Bipartisanship mean to you?" (5-8 sentences) To celebrate diversity and ensure equity and inclusivity, BPC is committed to: Recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce with insights and solutions for our increasingly divided society Creating a workplace culture where all employees feel valued and their perspectives are heard

item.title: Head Of Federal Legislative Affairs
item.description: Head of Federal Legislative Affairs Reports to: General Counsel & Head of Public Policy Location: Washington, DC Position Summary The Investment Adviser Association (IAA) seeks an experienced and strategic Head of Federal Legislative Affairs to lead the Association's federal legislative affairs function on behalf of the IAA and its investment adviser members. Reporting to the General Counsel & Head of Public Policy, the Head of Federal Legislative Affairs serves as the IAA's principal representative before Congress and a trusted resource for policymakers on issues affecting fiduciary investment advisers and their clients. The position leads the IAA's federal legislative affairs function as an integral part of the IAA's broader policy and advocacy program. Working closely with the President & CEO, the General Counsel & Head of Public Policy, and other stakeholders, the Head of Federal Legislative Affairs leads the IAA's day-to-day congressional advocacy, helping translate the IAA’s legislative policy positions into an effective congressional strategy and engagement program. The position is also responsible for enhancing the IAA's visibility, influence, and effectiveness on Capitol Hill, strengthening IAA-PAC through increased member participation, financial support, and engagement, and continually improving the IAA's legislative affairs function and member advocacy efforts. The IAA's advocacy is collaborative and integrated, bringing together legislative, regulatory, and public affairs perspectives to advance the Association's policy objectives. The successful candidate will exercise substantial independent judgment, uphold the highest ethical and professional standards, and thrive in a collegial environment by working effectively with colleagues at all levels of the IAA to ensure that the Association's legislative activities remain aligned with its broader advocacy strategy and organizational priorities. Primary Responsibilities Legislative Affairs and Congressional Relations Lead implementation of the IAA's legislative policy positions and congressional engagement strategy, working closely with IAA leadership, subject matter experts, IAA members, coalition partners, and the Association's outside public policy firm. Serve as the IAA’s principal representative before Congress, maintain registration as the IAA's federal lobbyist, and build and maintain a strong bipartisan and bicameral network of relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, and other organizations involved in the federal legislative process. Develop and carry out strategies to enhance the IAA's visibility, influence, and effectiveness on Capitol Hill and reinforce its reputation as a trusted, constructive, and nonpartisan resource for policymakers. Collaborate with IAA leadership to develop legislative policy positions and congressional strategy and engagement plans, and communicate their practical implications effectively to policymakers, IAA members, and other audiences. Anticipate and analyze legislative and political developments affecting investment advisers, identify emerging issues and opportunities, and develop strategies to address them. Develop and maintain a thorough understanding of the legal and regulatory framework governing the investment adviser industry. Serve as the IAA's primary day-to-day liaison with its outside public policy firm, conducting congressional outreach, advocacy initiatives, legislative monitoring, reporting, and execution of the IAA's legislative strategy. Lead the IAA’s congressional engagement efforts in coalitions and other collaborative initiatives and help ensure that legislative advocacy is coordinated with the Association's broader advocacy priorities. IAA Member Advocacy and Legislative Programs Lead the IAA's year-round IAA-member and grassroots advocacy efforts before Congress and, on occasion, state legislatures. Lead the IAA's principal legislative advocacy programs, including Advocacy Day, the Advocacy Council, and the legislative components of the annual Policy Forum, while continually identifying opportunities to strengthen their effectiveness, expand IAA member engagement, and increase their value to members. Develop legislative resources, communications, educational programming, advocacy materials, and other resources that help IAA members understand legislative developments and engage effectively with Congress, including authoring the IAA's weekly Five for Friday newsletter and other communications. Develop opportunities for meaningful year-round engagement between IAA members and Congress and support members in their direct advocacy efforts. IAA-PAC Serve as Secretary and Treasurer of IAA-PAC, providing strategic leadership for its governance, political engagement, fundraising, IAA member participation, and overall effectiveness. Oversee the day-to-day administration, compliance, and operations of IAA-PAC. Prepare materials, reports, and recommendations for the IAA-PAC Board regarding governance, political engagement, fundraising, and political contributions. Governance and Compliance Prepare materials and provide regular reports to the IAA Board of Governors and the IAA-PAC Board regarding legislative affairs activities, member advocacy initiatives, and IAA-PAC. Ensure compliance with applicable federal and state lobbying disclosure, campaign finance, and related political law requirements, including registrations, periodic reports, Federal Election Commission reporting, and other required filings. Qualifications and Personal Attributes Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or J.D. preferred. Approximately 8–12 years of progressively responsible experience in legislative affairs, congressional advocacy, government relations, or public policy. Demonstrated success developing and implementing congressional advocacy strategies and/or legislative initiatives, preferably involving financial services, securities, retirement, tax, appropriations, or related issues. Exceptional analytical, written, oral communication, public speaking, presentation, and organizational skills, including the ability to distill complex policy issues into clear, persuasive, and actionable messages for policymakers, IAA members, and other audiences. Demonstrated leadership, project management, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously, establish priorities, exercise sound professional and political judgment, and achieve results in a dynamic policy environment. Proven ability to build and maintain constructive bipartisan and bicameral relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, and others involved in the federal legislative process. Demonstrated integrity, professionalism, discretion, initiative, reliability, and strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust, collaborate effectively, and earn the confidence of colleagues, IAA members, policymakers, and external partners. Preferred Experience working for Congress, a financial services trade association, a lobbying or public policy consulting firm, or in a legislative affairs role at a federal regulatory agency. Familiarity with investment advisers, securities regulation, financial markets, and financial services policy. Experience administering a federal political action committee. Experience leading member engagement, grassroots advocacy, coalition activities, or congressional advocacy programs. Familiarity with the Lobbying Disclosure Act, the Federal Election Campaign Act, and related lobbying and campaign finance requirements. About the IAA The Investment Adviser Association is the leading association advancing the interests of fiduciary investment adviser firms. The IAA serves as the voice of the investment adviser community on key policy issues before Congress, the SEC, DOL CFTC, and other policymakers, and provides investment advisers with essential resources, connections, and opportunities to share best practices. The IAA’s member firms range from global asset managers to the medium- and small-sized firms that make up the majority of this industry. Collectively, our members manage more than $57 trillion in assets for a wide variety of clients, including individuals, families, trusts, investment companies, private funds, pension plans, state and local governments, endowments, corporations, and other institutional clients. Compensation and Benefits The compensation for this role reflects a broad range of factors, including relevant experience, expertise, and other considerations. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $250,000-$300,000 taking those factors into account. The IAA also provides a comprehensive benefits package for employees, including paid time off, paid holidays, medical, dental, and vision plans, a 401(k) plan with a generous company contribution, flexible savings accounts, long-term and short-term disability insurance, group life insurance, commuter benefits, and a hybrid work schedule. IAA is an Equal Opportunity Employer and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

item.title: Associate Government Affairs
item.description: Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Headquartered in Chicago, we develop, own, and operate large scale projects that power communities and support the energy future. This position will be open for application for at least 3 calendar days from the posting date. This position will remain open for application based on business need, which may be before or after the 3-day posting window. Position Overview As an Associate, Government Affairs – Central, you will focus on Invenergy's government affairs activities, primarily in the legislative and executive branch, across the Midwest. This position will support the overall Government Affairs initiatives and report to the Senior Manager, Government Affairs. You will work collaboratively with members of all departments within the company. In addition, this position requires an ability to work constructively with external stakeholders including trade organization leadership and staff, lobbyists, and peer companies. This position involves policy analysis, budgeting, preparing strategy documents, and weekly reporting. The position will be on-site at Invenergy's Chicago office. Responsibilities Support advocacy efforts across the region by developing relationships with necessary stakeholders and decisionmakers. Serve as a liaison with Invenergy contract lobbyists and direct their activities. Support coordination efforts with external stakeholders and interest groups to assist in achieving company objectives. Work closely with internal subject matter experts to develop positions on legislative proposals. Support efforts to develop and pass legislation to promote company objectives. Assist leadership in identifying potential legislative threats to the company. Communicate the Company’s position during trade organization meetings. Review statutory and regulatory requirements and develop comprehensive background reports on priority issues across key states. Minimum Qualifications 4+ years of relevant professional experience with 2+ years of legislative or energy related experience (i.e. utility, trade organization, government agency, independent power producer, etc.) Bachelor’s degree required. Ability to travel 30% of the time or as needed. Travel will ebb and flow based on legislative activity. Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future. Preferred Qualifications Strong written and verbal communication skills, comfortable in public speaking roles. Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to identify and solve problems. Able to maintain confidentiality of sensitive and proprietary information. $82,000.00 - $95,000.00 USD Annual Bonus: 20% - 30% The base pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target salary for the position. Invenergy considers a number of factors when determining base pay offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education and skills. item.description: We are a Firm where people truly believe in what they do and strive to achieve the highest standards of performance and success. This position is based in our Nashville office. General Description: We are seeking a Practice Assistant to join our team! Practice Assistants provide high-quality administrative support to a group of lawyers and professionals in a team environment, effectively and efficiently meeting Firm/client needs. Key Responsibilities and Essential Job Functions: This role serves as a trusted strategic partner to attorneys whose practice and community engagement involve frequent interaction with clients, corporate executives, board members, public officials, community leaders, and other high-profile stakeholders. Communicate effectively and professionally with clients, lawyers, and co-workers via email, by telephone, and in person; answer telephone, providing responses to routine questions from clients and staff members, and/or route calls to appropriate lawyers or staff member; arrange conference calls and greet clients. This role will manage complex and dynamic schedules, coordinate meetings and events, facilitate sensitive communications, oversee travel and logistics, and serve as a key point of contact for internal and external constituencies. Create, draft, format, edit, proofread, and manage Word documents, Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations; draft routine business correspondence, forms, and documents under the supervision of an appropriate lawyer/professional. Schedule domestic and foreign travel through Firm travel system, including flights, hotels, and/or car rentals. Prepare, organize, and process reimbursements, invoices, and check requests in a timely manner. Collect and prepare information to run conflict checks, open new client matters, and draft engagement letters, scope letters, and other required documents; provide guidance to lawyers to ensure completed forms are prepared and submitted properly. Learn client-specific billing guidelines or restrictions and consistently apply them to client invoices to ensure compliance and cost-effective practices. Open, prioritize, and distribute mail (both paper and electronic), coordinate mailings, deliveries, copying, scanning, and printing, when appropriate. Enter and manage work requests from lawyers in the Firm’s workflow tool and complete according to provided deadline(s). Perform routine electronic and paper filing in an organized manner for easy access; photocopy, scan, compile, and distribute documents; identify and coordinate available services provided by administrative departments, including office services, the IT Help Desk, document services, accounting, billing, and records. Perform all file maintenance, including saving documents to the document management system. Assist lawyers with time entry, billing, and collection, as needed. Operate independently to ensure completion of assignments, which may be complex in nature or require high-level production, in an accurate and timely manner. Produce a high volume of work assignments in an accurate and timely manner. Perform clerical duties for non-legal departments, as needed. Special projects and duties as assigned. Required Skills: Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite and Adobe. Experience with document management systems. Experience with electronic signature software programs. Proficiency in core legal administrative assistant functions and advanced technical and communications skills. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment with demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple competing tasks and demands. Superb attention to detail, grammar, and punctuation, and the ability to articulate thoughts and effectively present innovative ideas and findings. Ability to take direction and work independently with little supervision. Ability to effectively work well with others. Effective and professional interpersonal and communication skills. Ability to write clearly and professionally, with excellent proofing skills. Strong work ethic with ability and commitment to maintain confidentiality. Required Qualifications & Education: Bachelor's degree 4 – 5 years of experience supporting lawyers and paralegals with administrative or client-related tasks preferred. Physical Requirements: Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time. Moderate or advanced keyboard usage. Ability to lift and carry up to thirty pounds. Benefits: Our goal is to promote a work environment in which individuals have access to the resources they need to be their best both professionally and personally, which includes resources that encourage individuals to focus on their health and well-being. Below are the benefits we offer: comprehensive medical (PPO and HDHPs), dental and vision plans including coverage for domestic partners; life and AD&D insurance; short and long term disability insurance; tax-advantaged accounts for health care expenses, including FSAs and HSAs; FSAs for dependent care; health advocacy services; behavioral health and counseling resources for all family members; 401(k); profit sharing; backup dependent care; senior care planning support; resources for individuals with development disabilities and their caregivers; and paid holidays and other paid time off, including paid leave for new parents. item.description: Job Details: Cobb Poultry Selection Worker Three Springs Farm 17804 E 606 Rd Rose, OK 74364 Schedule : Monday through Thursday, including holidays. Hours : 5:00 am until 3:00 pm. Start and end times may vary. Work schedule is subject to change based upon production needs. Join the Cobb Family and Grow With Us! At Cobb, we’re passionate about helping our team members thrive—both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support you and your family in every stage of life. The best part- you’re eligible for benefits on day 1 of full-time hire! Starting Pay : $17.00 per hour plus additional shift differential for evenings, nights and weekends. What’s in it for you? Our competitive benefits include: Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance Short-Term & Long-Term Disability Free Telehealth Services Free Mental Health Services Well-Being Support Programs 401K & Stock Options Company Paid Life Insurance Free Education starting your first day on 175 -degree programs Citizenship Assistance Discounts on thousands of programs and services through Beneplace Additionally, we offer incentives such as Cobb Rewards, New Hire Referral and Referral Bonuses, Paid Vacations, Paid Holidays, Overtime Eligibility, and Earned Time Off. These are just a few of the ways we invest in YOU. Ready to take the next step? Apply today and become part of the Cobb family! Priority consideration will be provided to internal applicants first. Applicants with previous agricultural or production experience will be considered preferred. Applicants must reside in the United States to be considered for an interview. Requirements: Must have at least 6 months of consecutive work history with one employer and no additional job gaps in employment greater than 6 months in the past 36 months. If applicant has been laid off or providing child or elder care, the employment gap will be increased to 18 months. Previous work history will not apply to applicants who have been full time students consecutively for the last 36 months. Rehire criteria is a minimum waiting period of 180 days. Rehire Rule of no more than 3 times worked at Cobb/Tyson Foods. Company: Cobb Summary : Assisting with the selection of birds at approximately six weeks of age based on conformation, physical attributes, and family data; assisting with movement of birds within the complex. Other duties may be assigned. Essential Duties and Responsibilities : Assisting with the selection of up to 2500 pedigree birds daily by identifying gender, catching, scanning wing band number, and auditing market birds for wing bands. Monitoring ventilation and light. (35%) Assisting with properly identifying the coop birds are assigned to (30%) Maintaining clean foot pans in assigned boot room, sanitizing selection breakroom and all equipment used during selection process. Observing condition of farm structures and equipment and recommend needed maintenance and repairs. (15%) Assisting with setting up for selection by loading empty coops into house, placing catch frames in pens for easier bird access, hanging lights for better visual, setting up scales and scanner, making coop labels, placing coops in pens and running needed cords. Ensuring dead birds are disposed of properly each day at the end of selection (10%) Other duties, responsibilities, and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice, such as: assisting with moving birds from brood house to feed conversion or dissection and washing/disinfecting vehicles; properly euthanizing weak/ill birds in accordance with company policy (10%) Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements : The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines. Physical Demands and Work Environment : The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without reasonable accommodation. Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly lift and/or move, with assistance, up to 50 pounds (items such as bird coops, tables and tools). May be required to occasionally move up to 300 pounds such as stacks of bird coops. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift on multiple floor surfaces (i.e. concrete floor, shavings); walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects and controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; climb/ladder usage; stoop/bend up to 1000 times per day; talk or hear; drive a vehicle within the farm complex. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus. Environment: Required to work on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, extreme dusty, wet and cold environments. Personal Protective Equipment Required: Safety goggles, safety glasses, face shield, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, and company issued footwear are required. Ear plugs will be used as needed. NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators will be worn as needed. Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants such as Synergize, Virocid, Lysol, Bleach, hand sanitizer, Clorox wipes, etc. Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks. Relocation Assistance Eligible: No Work Shift: 1ST SHIFT (United States of America) Certain roles at Tyson require background checks. If you are offered a position that requires a background check you will be provided additional documentation to complete once an offer has been extended. Hourly Applicants ONLY -You must complete the task after submitting your application to provide additional information to be considered for employment. The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation. Tyson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, national origin, color, religion, age, genetics, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status. We provide our team members and their families with paid time off; 401(k) plans; affordable health, life, dental, vision and prescription drug benefits; and more. If you would like to learn more about your data privacy rights and how you may use that information, please read our Job Applicant Privacy Notice here . Unsolicited Assistance: Tyson Foods and its subsidiaries do not accept unsolicited support from external recruitment vendors for open positions within the United States. Any resumes or candidate profiles submitted by recruitment vendors or headhunters to any employee or applicant tracking system at Tyson Foods or its subsidiaries, without a valid written request and search agreement approved by HR, will be considered the property of Tyson Foods. No fees will be paid if the candidate is hired due to an unsolicited referral.

item.title: Sr Technical Program Manager Amazon Selection And Catalog Systems
item.description: Amazon Selection and Catalog Systems (ASCS) builds the systems that host and run the world’s largest e-Commerce products catalog. Within this organization the Product Knowledge and Browse Node Classification team is seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to drive solutions for classifying all products into the Catalog. The problem space consists on developing systems capable of identifying what a product is, mining product information to determine how a product across its different functions should be classified for browsing and searching purposes at high precision, scaling across marketplaces and languages. Key job responsibilities You will help build systems that are partially or entirely powered by AI and ML. The systems are responsible for handling continuous incoming traffic of products entering the catalog, building applications for analyzing product composition, mining product signals such as images, text and unstructured data to drive true understanding of product knowledge. As a TPM you will work to build solutions to real world problems, partnering closely with Scientists. The ideal candidate has worked on systems productionizing ML-based systems in one or several of the following fields: Web search, Deep Neural Networks, Classification Systems, Clustering, Natural Language Processing, Personalization, Artificial Intelligence. A successful candidate will have an established background in building innovative systems from inception to production, scaling systems with large data sets, developing customer-facing experiences, and making data-driven decisions. About the team The Product and Browse Node Classification team classifies products into the optimal Product Type, and Browse Node within Amazon’s Catalog and MP Taxonomy to ensure that they are discoverable when customers are searching or browsing. Owns Autoclassification systems, Misclassification detection, related services, interfaces and protections to reduce Seller contacts and friction. - 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience - 5+ years of technical product or program management experience - 3+ years of software development experience - Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules - 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience - Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules - Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner. The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits . USA, WA, Seattle - 148,700.00 - 201,200.00 USD annually

item.title: Public Policy Advocate
item.description: Job Title: Organizing & Advocacy Team, Public Policy Advocate Reports To: Senior Public Policy Manager Application Guidelines: First review of applications will occur on August 17 . Applications will be accepted until the position is filled. A cover letter is required for consideration. This position is currently hybrid. Out-of-state selected candidates will be required to relocate to the Oregon/SW Washington area before their date of hire and within 60 days of signing an offer letter . We recognize that people gain skills and experience in many different ways. If you’re excited about this role and believe you could succeed in it, we encourage you to apply — even if you do not meet every qualification listed. We especially welcome applications from people with lived experience related to hunger, poverty, and systemic inequities. Who We Are: Oregon Food Bank (OFB) believes that no one should be hungry. Our mission is to eliminate hunger and its root causes. We believe that food and health are basic human rights for all. We know that hunger is not just an individual experience; it is also a community-wide symptom of systemic barriers to employment, education, housing and health care such as systemic racism, sexism, and cissexism. That’s why we work systemically to achieve our mission to end hunger: we foster community connections to help people access nutritious food, and we build community power and strengthen networks of support and the safety net to eliminate the root causes of hunger for good. We build community power to dismantle systems and policies that drive hunger and poverty. Oregon Food Bank is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we strongly encourage applications from candidates who can increase the diversity of our organization and strengthen our capacity to eliminate hunger. We believe strongly in the power of lived experience — and we actively seek individuals who have experienced hunger and its root causes to join our team. Our organization is stronger because of the leadership of people who have faced food insecurity in their own lives and/or hail from historically under-represented communities. Learn more about our commitment at oregonfoodbank.org/equity . Who You Are: You care deeply about community, about people experiencing hunger and hold them in the center of all that you do. You are committed to apply equity as a process and an outcome of your work to disrupt systemic social patterns that promote hunger such as racism, sexism, and cissexism. You have a strong affinity with OFB’s 10 Year Vision and are profoundly excited to achieve this vision for and with our community. Position Summary: The Public Policy Advocate works to co-create, advocate for, and win proactive and high impact policy solutions rooted in the needs of our communities. The position ensures that OFB cultivates and sustains strategic relationships with elected officials primarily at the state level and is a lobbyist in the Oregon Legislature. Primary Responsibilities (Essential Functions): Together with our team of advocates and organizers, work collaboratively across OFB communities to develop and drive a high impact equity driven policy agenda supported by a vibrant and powerful community base. Manage a portfolio of issues relating to ending hunger and its root causes and represent OFB as a lobbyist in the Oregon Legislature. May organize grassroots campaigns to build public support for legislation or other OFB-supported causes. Develop and maintain effective relationships with legislators, policy advocates and community organizations pursuing an aligned OFB equity driven public policy agenda. Ensure that OFB cultivates and sustains strategic relationships with elected officials at the state level and relevant state agencies. Write policy analysis or other collateral to support engagement of multiple audiences. Act as spokesperson, when appropriate, to media or other audiences. Gains support from key stakeholders including members of the media or community leaders. Participate fully in OFB’s Advocacy, Volunteer and Organizing Team, share leadership across the team in peer to peer collaboration and team development. Participate fully in cross-department teams as assigned or as critical to position responsibilities. Participate fully in OFB’s organizational planning processes. Participate fully in data and technology systems by preparing reports that detail the status of bills or proposals, including lobbying activities and outcomes. Organizational level responsibilities of exempt employees include: To be an ambassador and a leader for OFB’s vision and mission, a cross-departmental collaborator, and an active contributor to building a movement to end hunger for good by addressing the root causes of hunger: systemic oppressions such as racism, xenophobia, sexism, and cisexism. In consultation and coordination with the supervisor, actively contribute to: cross-departmental efforts work culture activities and programming advisory and consultative groups such as the compensation committee, affinity groups, Equity Ambassadors, Equity Think Tank meetings, among others plan and engage in professional development activities that strengthen your capacity for your specific role as well as your capacity to contribute and advance organizational goals, OFB’s vision and mission. Identify, share, engage in, and collaboratively adjust and make necessary changes to this description of duties according to the inevitable evolution of the role over time. Skills and Experience Required: Deep passion for eliminating hunger and its root causes. 4+ years experience in public policy campaigns – legislative, electoral and administrative. 2+ years lobbying and/or government relations experience. Experience engaging communities in all phases of policy making. Demonstrated capacity to identify strategic opportunities for public policy change and leverage those opportunities into actionable campaigns that are mission and strategy aligned. Demonstrated excellence in conceptualizing project work plans and project managing from conception to evaluation. Demonstrated skill with researching, capturing, analyzing and reporting on scientific or technical concepts and information utilizing computerized applications, databases, spreadsheets and reports. Demonstrated expertise with research skills and with analyzing complex policy concepts related to food security, poverty, and economic insecurity through the lens of equity and racial justice —and to translate that analysis to multiple audiences. Excellent written and verbal communications. Ability to create persuasive arguments and strategies to influence positive outcomes in alignment with OFB mission, values and goals. Communicates diplomatically yet effectively with all audiences. Outstanding relationship building skills. Ability to develop and maintain relationships in the context of building relationships for the organization and its mission. Demonstrated ability to navigate conflict through effective leadership and problem-solving and ability to handle sensitive information effectively and confidentially. Ability to travel to Salem during legislative sessions full-time or as-needed. Ability to travel within and outside of Oregon up to 4 days at a time up to 4 times per year. Organizational level skills and experience required for exempt employees include: Disposition and willingness to maximize multiple perspectives to innovate, problem solve and seek creative solutions. Experience in modeling intercultural competence and demonstrated commitment to equity and social justice. Demonstrated ability to think strategically, collaborate, take initiative, and to maintain confidentiality. Project coordination and organization skills; ability to manage multiple projects with attention to detail; ability to handle interruptions, and produce timely, accurate work. Ability to both work independently and as part of a team; comfortable working in an office environment and offsite. Ability to thrive in a diverse, creative, responsive, mission-driven, and fast-paced work culture. Experience of successful multicultural immersion working and/or living within OFB's Equity Constituencies: BIPoC, Immigrants & Refugees, Single Mothers, Trans and Gender-Non-Conforming folx. Multicultural Immersion defined as: Actively integrated in one or more communities, interacting with individuals and groups, and seeking to understand the diversities within and between communities by being there and engaging in daily life activities. Preferred Qualifications: Personal lived-experience of systemic hunger and/or its root causes (racism, sexism, heterosexism, cis-sexism, ableism, ageism, size-ism, ethnocentrism, and classism) Organizational level preferred qualifications of exempt employees include: Multilingual skills at a minimum professional level of proficiency or greater in English and any additional language/s, defined as being able to speak the languages with sufficient structural accuracy and vocabulary to participate effectively in most formal and informal conversations on practical and professional topics. Multicultural skills of adaptation and integration are strongly preferred. Adaptation is defined as the capacity to communicate and interact with people of multiple cultures, backgrounds, and styles by incorporating and adapting to the world view and perspectives of others. Integration is defined as being able to “code-switch” or move in and out of one's worldview and help others understand different cultures, backgrounds, and styles to promote diversity and inclusion. Commitment to continued professional development to strengthen capacity to work through an equity lens for equity and racial justice. Strong capacity to consider multiple perspectives, to pivot to respond to emerging needs and lead through organizational changes. Years of successful multicultural immersion either working with and/or living within one or more of OFB’s

item.title: Manager Public Policy
item.description: The Manager, Public Policy will develop and execute advocacy strategies and policy initiatives in support of Amazon's policy priorities related to trade and customs. The Manager will work closely with other public policy teams, Legal, PR, and the relevant business units to ensure alignment with business priorities and goals. Key job responsibilities - Engage with U.S. policymakers on trade and customs issues and develop broad government relations strategies. - Leverage expert understanding of the U.S. legislative and regulatory policymaking processes to advance Amazon's policy priorities. - Create factual, relevant, and easily understandable talking points and other messaging, and persuasively deliver them to relevant audiences. - Analyze technical language in legislative and regulatory proposals, identify potential impacts on corporate operations, and synthesize policy documents for internal customers. - Build and maintain relationships with trade associations, think tanks, advocacy groups, and other relevant external stakeholders to advance public policy objectives. - An ability and desire to travel is required. About the team This role sits within the Public Policy Americas team and will work collaboratively across other public policy teams, Legal, PR, and relevant business units to support policy priorities related to trade and customs. The Manager will report to the Senior Manager, Public Policy. - Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline (e.g. Law, Political Science, Public Policy, Public Affairs, Economic Development) - 8+ years of relevant public policy experience, including direct involvement in legislative processes and government relations. - J.D., or Master's degree - Highly effective communication skills and experience translating complex policy issues into written materials for diverse audiences (e.g., briefing documents, testimony, public comment letters). - Demonstrated ability to effectively and comfortably interact and engage at the highest corporate, legislative, regulatory agency, and other government levels. - Ability to be flexible and demonstrate strong judgment/decision-making skills and political acumen. - Ability to maintain the highest personal levels of ethical conduct, confidentiality, and integrity in all engagements. item.title: Senior Counsel Legislative Regulatory Affairs
item.description: Since opening our first self-storage facility in 1972, Public Storage has grown to become the largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities in the world. With thousands of locations across the U.S. and Europe, and more than 170 million net rentable square feet of real estate, we're also one of the largest landlords. We've been recognized as A Great Place to Work by the Great Place to Work Institute. And, our employees have also voted us as having Best Career Growth , ranked us in the Top 5% for Work Culture , and in the Top 10% for Diversity and Inclusion . We're a member of the S&P 500 and FT Global 500 . Our common and preferred stocks trade on the New York Stock Exchange. Public Storage is the nation’s leading self-storage provider, recognized for its iconic orange doors and commitment to delivering simple, reliable solutions to millions of customers across the country. We are expanding our creative team to enhance our consistent and engaging visual brand presence. Public Storage is seeking a Senior Counsel / Counsel, Legislative & Regulatory Affairs to help lead the company’s response to an increasingly complex legislative and regulatory environment. This is a new, highly visible role supporting a national consumer-facing business at a time of significant growth, regulatory scrutiny, and operational complexity. This individual will work closely with Legal, Operations, Compliance, Revenue Management, Marketing, Call Center, Insurance/Risk, and senior business leaders to monitor, interpret, and help shape legislative and regulatory developments affecting Public Storage and the self-storage industry. You will engage in regulatory advocacy, state and federal rulemaking, legislative strategy, trade association work/engagement, and other government-facing matters. The ideal candidate will bring strong legal judgment and a working understanding of how legislative and regulatory processes affect business operations. This role is well suited for someone who enjoys working across legal, business, and policy issues; can move comfortably between detail-oriented statutory analysis and executive-level guidance; and wants to help build a scalable legislative and regulatory affairs function for a national business. The role will support strategy in areas including consumer protection, pricing, advertising/marketing, operations, competition issues, and state self-storage laws. Key Responsibilities Monitor, assess, and advise on federal, state, and local legislative and regulatory developments affecting Public Storage and the self-storage industry. Help develop and execute advocacy strategies on legislation, rulemaking, regulatory proposals, and other government-facing matters. Suggest alternative language, exceptions, and modifications to material legislation and coordinate with lobbyists, trade associations, outside counsel, consultants, and other external resources. Partner with internal stakeholders to evaluate operational impact and develop practical compliance strategies. Support company responses to proposed legislation, rulemaking activity, regulatory inquiries, and other government-facing matters. Work with trade associations, outside counsel, consultants, and government affairs to advance the company’s legislative and regulatory priorities. Translate complex legal and regulatory developments into clear, actionable guidance for business leaders. Support integration and compliance planning related to acquisitions, new jurisdictions, and business expansion. Advise on emerging issues involving consumer protection, pricing, marketing, operations, call center practices, lien laws, insurance/risk, and related regulatory matters. Help build scalable processes for tracking, escalating, and responding to legislative and regulatory developments. Qualifications 8+ years of relevant legal, legislative, regulatory, government affairs, or public policy experience. Experience with, or willingness to develop familiarity with, campaign finance, lobbying, gift, ethics, and related political law requirements. Experience interpreting statutes, regulations, proposed legislation, administrative rules, and regulatory guidance. Experience working with or before legislatures, regulators, attorneys general, agencies, trade associations, or government affairs organizations. Strong judgment, executive presence, and ability to advise senior business leaders. Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, multi-jurisdictional environment. Practical, business-oriented approach to legal and regulatory risk. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to develop subject-matter expertise in new and evolving regulatory areas. Preferred Qualifications J.D. from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing. Workplace One of our values pillars is to work as One Team and we believe that there is no replacement for in-person collaboration but understand the value of some flexibility. Public Storage teammates are expected to work in the office five days each week with the option to take up to three flexible remote days per month. Public Storage is an equal opportunity employer and embraces diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply. **Sponsorship for Work Authorization is not available for this posting. Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without restrictions or requiring sponsorship now or in the future. We do not provide training plans or support for F-1 OPT, STEM OPT extensions, or future visa sponsorship.**

item.title: Legislative Intern
item.description: Company Name: Texas Farm Bureau | Department: Government Affairs Texas Farm Bureau is a membership organization that is committed to successfully advancing the public policy interests of farmers and ranchers. The intern will work in the Texas Farm Bureau State Legislative Office (located in Austin, Texas) during the 2027 Regular Session of the Texas Legislature. In this role, they will work closely with the Government Affairs team to support legislative initiatives that advance Texas agricultural producers and rural communities. In doing so, they will gain valuable experience in the legislative process and see the impact of membership organizations. The intern will also have the opportunity to assist with the Texas Agriculture Council (TAC) throughout the legislative session, enabling them to maximize networking opportunities and develop lasting professional connections within Texas' legislative and agricultural advocacy communities. TAC is a collaborative network of agricultural advocacy organizations that coordinates policy and advocacy efforts and facilitates information sharing on issues affecting the agricultural community. This role provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the state legislative process. Creating an opportunity for exposure to public policy, state government, and advocacy, while building professional skills. MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES AND AUTHORITY Researching high-profile legislative and policy issues shaping the future of Texas agriculture. Tracking legislation and monitoring committee hearings, legislative meetings, and policy developments at the Texas Capitol. Creating briefing materials, presentations, and advocacy resources used to engage legislators, stakeholders, and agricultural leaders. Writing bill summaries, policy briefs, and legislative communications, including content for Texas Farm Bureau's weekly Austin Newsletter. Utilizing legislative tracking tools and databases to provide real-time updates and support strategic advocacy efforts. Providing support to the Texas Agriculture Council (TAC) by coordinating and preparing materials for weekly meetings, managing logistics, and scheduling guest speakers. The guest speakers include but are not limited to members of the Legislature, legislative staff, stakeholders, and industry professionals. Maintaining TAC legislative bill tracking reports and assisting with the implementation of TAC action items. Preparing materials for weekly TAC meetings and special events, promoting agricultural issues and priorities among legislators and staff Performing other duties as assigned. MINIMUM POSITION REQUIREMENTS Availability to be in Austin, Texas during the duration of the regular session of the 90th Texas Legislature (January 12, 2027-June 4, 2027). Practical knowledge of production agriculture and rural issues Current undergraduate student or recent graduate Good organizational skills Ability and willingness to learn and extend skills Good oral and written communication skills Interest in public policy issues, including but not limited to agriculture, property rights, environmental regulations, water policy, preferred PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Repeated use of PC, telephone, and office machines. Extended periods of sitting and concentrating. Occasional bending, twisting, crouching, pulling, pushing and reaching in an office environment. Occasional lifting and moving items weighing up to 30 lbs. WORKING CONDITIONS Occasional long, irregular work hours. Travel as required. Work to be conducted in office environment owned or leased by company

item.title: Legislative Legal Intern
item.description: Company Name: Texas Farm Bureau | Department: Government Affairs To support the Texas Farm Bureau State Legislative Office in Austin Texas during the 2027 Regular Session of the Texas Legislature. This position provides a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience with the legislative process while developing practical skills in legal research, policy analysis, legislative drafting, and advocacy. The Legal Intern will work closely with the Government Affairs team to support legislative initiatives that advance Texas agriculture and rural communities. MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES AND AUTHORITY Conducting legal and policy research on proposed legislation, regulatory matters, and emerging issues affecting agriculture. Reviewing, analyzing, and tracking legislation throughout the legislative process. Preparing bill summaries, policy analyses, and legislative briefing materials for Texas Farm Bureau staff and leadership. Drafting legislative correspondence, member communications, and content for the weekly Austin Newsletter distributed to Texas Farm Bureau members. Attending and monitoring committee hearings, legislative meetings, and other Capitol proceedings. Assisting in the development of legislative strategy by monitoring policy developments and preparing testimony, presentations, and advocacy materials. Assisting with and independently drafting legislative amendments, bill language, legislative memoranda, and other legislative documents under the supervision of the Government Affairs team. Collaborating with legislators, legislative staff, stakeholders, and industry leaders on issues impacting Texas agriculture. Performing other duties as assigned. MINIMUM POSITION QUALIFICATIONS Availability to be in Austin, Texas during the duration of the regular session of the 90th Texas Legislature (January 12, 2027-May 31, 2027). Knowledge of production agriculture and rural issues. Current Law student classified as 2L or 3L. Good organizational skills. Ability and willingness to learn and extend skills. Good verbal and written communication skills. Excellent punctuality and attendance. Ability to prioritize and handle time sensitive matters. Interest in public policy issues, including but not limited to property rights, environmental regulations, water policy, administrative law, and agricultural law, preferred. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS Repeated use of PC, telephone, and office machines. Extended periods of sitting and concentrating. Occasional bending, twisting, crouching, pulling, pushing and reaching in an office environment. Occasional lifting and moving items weighing up to 30 lbs. WORKING CONDITIONS Occasional long, irregular work hours. Travel as required.
